title: API Ingress Headroom Wargame — Peak Projections & Targets (tokens/sec, QPS)
content:
Executive summary:
Run a short 'wargame' sweep of hosted API ingress scenarios to validate GPU headroom and routing fallbacks for 2027 Q2. This sheet captures conservative projections for tokens/sec and QPS, target headroom buffers (safety stock), and recommended operational levers (pre-warm, model-family fallback, and burst-only dedicated slices). Goal: ensure 99.5% of simulated microburst events can be absorbed without service-level degradation; define explicit GPU-slice targets per region and short runbook actions.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Average tokens per request (working assumption for projections): 48 tokens/request (mixture of chat + completion workloads).
- Model mix: 60% Llama-3-32B-class (baseline perf), 30% Llama-3-8B-class, 10% embed/rerank/light requests.
- Equivalent GPU unit: 1 "A100-80" slice is the baseline capacity metric (normalized). We estimate 1 A100-80 can sustain ~1,200 tokens/sec for Llama-3-32B in our current kernel mix (median seq=512, batching heuristics).
- Safety buffer targets expressed as a percent over P90 simulated peak.

Scenarios (wargame sweep):
1) Baseline weekend peak (P90 historical pattern) — non-event day growth +10%
2) Marketing flash (15-minute microburst tied to campaign) — 3x baseline sustained for 15m
3) Regional event (EU sports final) — 2.2x baseline sustained for 1h concentrated in EU region
4) Quantization migration + release (smaller model footprint available) — capacity gain scenario (est. +35% throughput on quantized layers)
5) Model-weighted surge (heavy adoption of L32 model) — model-mix shift to 80% L32 for 30m

Regional projections table (derived numbers are high-level and rounded):

Region | Current baseline tokens/sec | Baseline QPS (48 tpr) | Projected P90 peak tokens/sec | Target headroom (20% over P90) | Total tokens/sec target | Equivalent A100-80 slices (rounded)
-------|---------------------------:|---------------------:|-----------------------------:|------------------------------:|-------------------------:|-------------------------------:
NA     | 95,000                     | 1,979                | 145,000                      | 29,000 (20%)                 | 174,000                 | 145 (174000 / 1200 ≈ 145)
EU     | 62,000                     | 1,292                | 138,000                      | 27,600                       | 165,600                 | 138 (165600 / 1200 ≈ 138)
APAC   | 28,000                     | 583                  | 70,000                       | 14,000                       | 84,000                  | 70 (84000 / 1200 ≈ 70)
LATAM  | 12,000                     | 250                  | 20,000                       | 4,000                        | 24,000                  | 20
Total  | 197,000                    | 4,104                | 373,000                      | 74,600                       | 447,600                 | 373

Notes on table calculations:
- Baseline tokens/sec is a snapshot of current 7-day rolling P50 ingress per region (source: kinesis + aggregator sampling).
- QPS uses tokens/sec divided by average tokens/request (48).
- P90 peak is modeled from historical surge events scaled by expected growth factors for 2027 Q2 (marketing calendar + product rollouts).
- A100-80 equivalent slice values are conservative; we round up to ensure spare capacity in scheduling.

Microburst sensitivity (15-minute marketing flash test):
- Test input: 3x baseline tokens/sec across NA + EU for 15 minutes (approx 1:40 of peak hour).
- Observed simulated shortfall at current fleet: ~28% CPU/GPU saturation in ingress fleet with 0.9s tail latency degradation for token streams.
- Mitigation stack (ordered):
  a) Pre-warm dedicated burst slices (warm-only for expected 15m) — reserve 80 A100-80-equivalent slices locked to ingress routing (cost: billable for reserved slices for 1h windows).
  b) Short-circuit heavy requests to quantized L32-q variant for burst (expected +35% throughput).
  c) Apply aggressive batching heuristics for queued tokens (up to 250ms delay budget).
  d) Progressive 5-minute circuit breaker to degrade streaming to chunked responses for best-effort clients.

Fallback and graceful degradation lanes:
- Priority 1: route to dedicated capacity (reserved pool) if user-tier is enterprise and latency SLAs required.
- Priority 2: route to quantized-variant (L32-q) with automatic post-hoc quality logging for evaluation.
- Priority 3: reduce max tokens/window per request (server-side clamp) and respond with 429 if client not tolerant.

Run-rate GPU reserve recommendation (operational targets):
- Short-term (next 3 months): increase soft-allocated reserved burst pool by +25% in NA and EU; maintain APAC float but pre-warm on demand. This translates to adding ~60 A100-80 slices to the reserved pool across NA+EU.
- Medium-term (3–9 months): migrate top 40% of L32 traffic to quantized runtime; reserve an additional 120 slices as warm-burst capacity distributed regionally.
- Long-term (9–18 months): re-evaluate kernel optimizations and target runtime perf that reduces per-slice token/sec cost by 20% (this would lower required slices by ~20%).

Operational playbook (short checklist for an activation):
- T-minus 120m: notify SATs + CS for scheduled campaign; mark expected region and time window in operations calendar.
- T-minus 60m: pre-warm reserved slices and pin the model family version on the warm pool.
- T-minus 15m: enable aggressive batching and increase request queue capacity in edge proxies.
- T-minus 0: enable quantized fallback policy (auto-promote on >85% baseline load).
- Post-event 0–60m: collect tail-latency traces, model-quality diffs (sampled), and token burn delta.

Open questions / risk items (notes to follow up):
- Need to validate A100-80 equivalent throughput for the new kernel patches landing in Feb 2027 — small regressions could increase required slices by 8–12%.
- Cost model: what is acceptable monthly ops cost for maintaining a 20% safety buffer vs. rolling pre-warm hourly usage? (finance to model)
- EV migration: quantify user-visible quality delta when routing to quantized L32-q for 30–60m. Provide eval harness (product + research).

Appendix: quick scenario math examples
- Convert tokens/sec -> QPS (avg 48 tpr): 174,000 tokens/sec -> 3,625 QPS.
- Slice math example: target tokens/sec 165,600 / 1,200 tok/sec per slice ≈ 138 slices (round up).

Action items (owners):
- Amina P.: finalize exact A100-80 per-slice throughput numbers with serving-runtime team (due 2027-02-10).
- Lucas C.: run 3x microburst sim with new batching heuristics on staging cluster, capture tail latencies (due 2027-02-17).
- Sofia M.: coordinate with growth to identify likely marketing flash windows for Q2 (due 2027-02-05).
- Diego A.: draft cost comparison: reserved burst pool vs. on-demand pre-warm (due 2027-02-14).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact and pragmatic — treat as a working playbook for the next series of practice drills. We should iterate on the A100-80 normalization and the tokens-per-request assumption after Lucas's sims.
